claim.title: Grokking time distribution bimodality
claim.statement: In the D-dimensional uniform ball model limit ($\lambda_2 \ll \epsilon^2$), the grokking time PDF is bimodal, consisting of a continuous distribution for fast relaxation and a Dirac delta peak for slow relaxation.
claim.test_plan: Simulate the D-dimensional ball model with parameters $D=5, \epsilon=2, \lambda_2=0.01$ (as in Fig 9). Run 10,000 trials with random initial weights $w(0) \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I)$. Record the grokking time $t_G$ for each trial that groks. Plot the histogram of $t_G$. Pass if the histogram shows two distinct modes: a broad distribution at smaller $t_G$ and a sharp peak (or cluster of values) at a larger, specific $t_G$ corresponding to the slow relaxation time $t_G = \frac{1}{2\lambda_{2,D}}\ln(\frac{\epsilon^4}{\epsilon^4-1})$.
claim.evidence_in_paper: Section 3.3.3: 'By combining the grokking-time PDFs for the fast and the slow relaxation we obtain the grokking-time PDF... In Fig. 9 we show the grokking-time PDFs... The Dirac-delta long-relaxation grokking time is represented by vertical bars.'
claim.success_criterion: The empirical distribution of grokking times exhibits two distinct clusters/modes, with one mode centered near the analytically predicted slow-relaxation time.
